what: CCC Intelligent Solutions provides software that runs the US auto insurance claims process. When a car is damaged, insurers, repair shops, parts suppliers and lenders all use CCC’s cloud platform to estimate the repair, order parts and settle the claim, increasingly with AI that reads photos of the damage.
customers: Auto insurers (most of the top US carriers), about 30,000 collision repair shops, parts suppliers and car makers.
money: Claims and estimating software for insurers.
Parts ordering, casualty claims and other network products.
moat: A network: insurers use CCC because repair shops do, and the reverse. That makes it the industry standard and very hard to displace. Customers sign multi-year contracts, so revenue is predictable.
risks: GAAP earnings are depressed by stock compensation and amortisation, so the P/E of 64 is misleading.
Growth depends on selling more products into a mature customer base.
Fewer accidents, for example from safer cars, would reduce claim volumes over time.
opportunities: Revenue has grown every year, from $688M in 2021 to $1.14B over the last twelve months.
Free cash flow grew from $89M to $311M over the same period.
AI damage estimation from photos speeds up claims and is a natural upsell.
The forward P/E of about 15 on adjusted earnings is low for a dominant software network.
watch: Revenue growth from new products, especially AI-based estimating, and free cash flow per share.
view: CCC is the industry standard for car insurance claims in the US, and that kind of network rarely loses its position. Revenue has grown every year and free cash flow has more than tripled since 2021, to $311 million over the last twelve months.

The GAAP P/E of 64 says little because of stock compensation and amortisation; on free cash flow the market value of about $4.6 billion is roughly 15 times. That is cheap for software with this kind of position, and reflects concerns that growth is slowing and that AI might let new entrants disrupt estimating.

This turns on whether CCC can keep selling new products to insurers and repair shops. I think its network makes it more likely to win the AI shift than to lose it, and at 15 times free cash flow the shares look attractive to me.
bull: AI products drive faster growth and the market re-rates a dominant software network.
bear: Growth slows to low single digits and the shares stay cheap.
